Adequacy radius (heterogeneity tolerance) of a stepped-wedge design

Source: R/stepped_wedge.R
sw_radius.Rd

\(\kappa^* = \eta_{\alpha,\epsilon} / \{(z_{1-\alpha/2} + z_{power})\Gamma\}\): the largest RMS exposure-time heterogeneity, relative to the planned effect, at which the worst-case coverage of the nominal \(1-\alpha\) IT interval falls by at most \(\epsilon\), for a trial planned with the stated power against a constant effect.

Usage

sw_radius(
  W = NULL,
  design = NULL,
  target = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05,
  epsilon = 0.05,
  power = 0.8,
  ...
)

Arguments

W

exposure weights (as from [sw_exposure_weights()]); alternatively supply design and the covariance arguments in ...

design

optional design, passed with ... to [sw_exposure_weights()]

target

target weights \(v\) summing to one; default TATE (\(v = 1/L\))

alpha, epsilon

test level and tolerated coverage loss (defaults 0.05)

power

planned power (default 0.80)

...

covariance and estimator arguments for [sw_exposure_weights()]

Value

\(\kappa^*\) (0.2329 / \(\Gamma\) at the defaults)

Examples

sw_radius(design = c(6, 6, 6, 6, 0), phi = 2)    # 0.133
#> [1] 0.1332467
sw_radius(design = c(4, 4, 4, 4, 8), phi = 2)    # 0.214
#> [1] 0.2143148
